args.Message: **CERVICAL SPECIAL TESTS** --- **1 Spurlings Test /Foraminal Compression Test/** **PURPOSE** To assess cervical nerve root compression /cervical radiculopathy/ **PROCEDURE** • Patient sits comfortably • Extend laterally flex and rotate the head towards the affected side • Apply gentle downward compression on the head **POSITIVE SIGN** Radiating pain numbness or tingling into the upper limb **INDICATES** • Cervical nerve root compression • Cervical radiculopathy --- **2 Cervical Distraction Test** **PURPOSE** To assess cervical nerve root compression **PROCEDURE** • Patient lies supine • Therapist gently grasps the head and applies an upward traction force **POSITIVE SIGN** Relief of neck or arm pain **INDICATES** • Cervical radiculopathy • Foraminal compression --- **3 Upper Limb Tension Test /ULTT/** **PURPOSE** To assess neural tissue mobility and detect peripheral nerve or cervical nerve root involvement --- **ULTT 1 /MEDIAN NERVE BIAS/** **Procedure** • Depress the shoulder • Abduct the shoulder to 110 • Supinate the forearm • Extend the wrist and fingers • Externally rotate the shoulder • Slowly extend the elbow • Finally side flex the neck away if required **Positive Sign** • Pain tingling or numbness along the median nerve distribution • Difference in symptoms compared to the opposite side **Indicates** • Median nerve tension • Cervical radiculopathy --- **ULTT 2A /MEDIAN NERVE BIAS/** **Procedure** • Shoulder depression • Elbow extension • External rotation of shoulder • Forearm supination • Wrist and finger extension **Positive Sign** Reproduction of median nerve symptoms **Indicates** Median nerve irritation --- **ULTT 2B /RADIAL NERVE BIAS/** **Procedure** • Shoulder depression • Internal rotation of shoulder • Elbow extension • Forearm pronation • Wrist finger and thumb flexion with ulnar deviation **Positive Sign** Pain or tingling along the dorsolateral forearm and hand **Indicates** Radial nerve tension --- **ULTT 3 /ULNAR NERVE BIAS/** **Procedure** • Shoulder depression • Shoulder abduction and external rotation • Elbow flexion • Forearm pronation • Wrist extension with radial deviation • Finger extension **Positive Sign** Pain or tingling along the medial forearm and little finger **Indicates** Ulnar nerve tension --- **4 Vertebral Artery Test** **PURPOSE** To assess vertebrobasilar insufficiency before cervical mobilization or manipulation **PROCEDURE** • Patient lies supine • Therapist extends rotates and laterally flexes the neck • Hold for about 30 seconds while observing symptoms **POSITIVE SIGN** • Dizziness • Vertigo • Nystagmus • Blurred vision • Nausea **INDICATES** Vertebrobasilar insufficiency **Precaution** Stop the test immediately if symptoms appear --- **SPECIAL EXAMINATION TESTS** --- **1 DIZZINESS TEST** **PURPOSE** To assess for cervical vascular compromise/vertebrobasilar insufficiency that may produce dizziness during cervical movement **PROCEDURE** • Patient is positioned sitting • Examiner stabilizes the patients head • Slowly place the cervical spine into extension and rotation • Observe the patient for symptoms **POSITIVE SIGN** • Dizziness • Vertigo • Nausea • Visual disturbance • Nystagmus **INDICATES** Possible vertebrobasilar insufficiency and requires further medical evaluation --- **2 SHOULDER DEPRESSION TEST** **PURPOSE** To assess nerve root/nerve tissue irritation or shortening of neural structures in the cervical and upper limb region **PROCEDURE** • Patient is sitting • Examiner stabilizes/depresses the shoulder on the tested side • Passively side flex the patients neck away from the tested side • The position places tension on the cervical nerve structures **POSITIVE SIGN** • Reproduction of the patients radiating pain/paresthesia into the upper limb **INDICATES** Possible cervical nerve root or brachial plexus involvement --- **3 PINCH GRIP TEST** **PURPOSE** To assess the function of the anterior interosseous nerve /AIN/ and flexor pollicis longus/index FDP function **PROCEDURE** • Ask the patient to make a pinch/OK sign by touching the tip of the thumb to the tip of the index finger • Observe the shape of the circle formed **POSITIVE SIGN** • Patient cannot make a proper round OK circle • Instead the pinch becomes flattened/pulp to pulp **INDICATES** Anterior interosseous nerve palsy/dysfunction --- **4 CARPAL COMPRESSION TEST** **PURPOSE** To assess for carpal tunnel syndrome due to median nerve compression **PROCEDURE** • Patients wrist is in a neutral position • Examiner applies direct pressure over the carpal tunnel with the thumbs/fingers • Maintain pressure for approximately 30 seconds **POSITIVE SIGN** • Reproduction of • Pain • Tingling • Numbness • Paresthesia in the median nerve distribution **INDICATES** Carpal Tunnel Syndrome / median nerve compression --- **5 HAND ELEVATION TEST** **PURPOSE** To assess for carpal tunnel syndrome/median nerve compression **PROCEDURE** • Patient raises both hands above the head • Maintain the elevated position for approximately 1 2 minutes • Ask the patient about symptoms **POSITIVE SIGN** • Reproduction of pain numbness or tingling in the median nerve distribution **INDICATES** Possible Carpal Tunnel Syndrome --- **6 FROMENTS SIGN** **PURPOSE** To assess the ulnar nerve particularly the function of adductor pollicis **PROCEDURE** • Ask the patient to hold a piece of paper between the thumb and index finger • Examiner attempts to pull the paper away **POSITIVE SIGN** Patient compensates by • Flexing the IP joint of the thumb using flexor pollicis longus **INDICATES** Ulnar nerve palsy/weakness of adductor pollicis
